convoLines.text: "Why do you ask? What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now. Don't waste it."
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? This isn't new."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The whole fire was arguing about Highbeam Deer last night — what to even CALL it. 'Sir Blinds-A-Lot' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Tbilisi, Georgia mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now."
"Still on your regrets."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Hm."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Highbeam Deer? Carol is pushing 'Old Stare'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hah. Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"I don't talk about that. Not because it's secret — because saying it out loud makes it real in a way I can't afford yet. Someday. Not today."
"Still on who you left behind."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I dreamed Claire was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
They light up a little when they see you.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening. That's where we are."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"My part? I count portions out loud before eating and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"You wanted one full night's sleep — no waking up listening. Had it yet?"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Klaus doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? Simple as that."

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about Inspiration last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Big Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"This one — Salmonberry. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Vancouver, Canada. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything. Funny how that works."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Linh is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sleep's gone strange. I greet everyone by name each morning at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said yes — you left someone behind. I never asked who. I won't. But I'm still here, asking nothing, if that helps."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff. — or so they tell me."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
